The three boundary lines are respectively y=3-x, y=x+1, y=3x-5. Find the pairwise intersection points: from y=3-x and y=x+1, obtain x=1,y=2, that is (1,2); from y=x+1 and y=3x-5, obtain x=3,y=4, that is (3,4); from y=3-x and y=3x-5, obtain x=2,y=1, that is (2,1). These three points all satisfy the corresponding third inequality, so the region M is a triangle with vertices (1,2), (3,4), (2,1). If the line y=kx passes through a point (x,y) inside M, then k=y/x. The abscissas of the three vertices are all positive, therefore on this convex triangle, the range of values of y/x is determined by the minimum value and maximum value at the vertices. Calculate the vertex slopes: at (1,2), k=2/1=2; at (3,4), k=4/3; at (2,1), k=1/2. Therefore the minimum value is 1/2, the maximum value is 2, and the boundary is included in the region, so the range of values of k is [1/2,2].
